newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss president proposes big humanitarian fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss president proposes big humanitarian fund.

text.p: Swiss President Arnold Koller proposed on Wednesday creating a huge humanitarian fund that would use Swiss official gold reserves to aid victims of human rights abuses, catastrophes and the Holocaust.

The "Swiss Foundation for Solidarity", to be set up next year, could administer around seven billion Swiss francs ($4.7 billion) in funds freed up by reform of Swiss official reserves, Koller told a special joint session of parliament.

"The Federal Council (cabinet), in accord with the Swiss National Bank and with an eye on the anniversary year of 1998, has developed the idea of a Swiss Foundation for Solidarity," Koller said in a speech on Switzerland's World War Two role.
He said the foundation could be financed by making more efficient use of the country's gold reserves, a process that will take some time and require amending the Swiss constitution.

It could generate a few hundred million francs (dollars) a year in revenue to be split in half among needy recipients in Switzerland and abroad. They could include "victims of poverty and catastrophes, of genocide and other serious human rights abuses, of course also for those of the Holocaust and Shoa."

If the plan is adopted, the government would not contribute any public funds to a Holocaust memorial fund, as is now being considered. Big banks have already donated 100 million francs ($67 million) to the fund. The Swiss National Bank plans to contribute 100 million francs as well, Koller said.
